claims.text: Formation of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles with more than five elements is governed by precursor mobility.
Crystal-structure selection in these nanoparticles is governed by thermodynamic stability.
Precursor mobility and thermodynamic stability can be controlled by characterizing the system in situ and manipulating synthesis conditions.
The relevant initial material is a single-phase solid solution.
Heating and cooling rates will be varied as the controlled synthesis intervention.
The applicable processing regime involves rapid heating and cooling.
Precursor mobility and thermodynamic stability are the structural mediators of crystal-structure selection.
Stochastic principles govern formation of the single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Controlled variation of synthesis conditions will improve control over crystal structure.
Controlled variation of synthesis conditions will reduce phase separation and elemental segregation.
Controlled variation of synthesis conditions will reduce uncontrolled particle morphology.
The baseline exhibits uncontrolled crystal structure, phase separation, elemental segregation, uncontrolled particle morphology, and high thermal decomposition temperatures.
The compositional boundary is a noble metal-based alloy containing more than five elements.
The processing boundary is a rapid-heating and rapid-cooling synthesis regime.
The relationship among precursor mobility, thermodynamic stability, and crystal-structure selection is not well understood.
Failure of synthesis-condition variation to improve crystal-structure control or reduce phase separation, segregation, and morphology variability would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as a single-phase solid solution, while the baseline is described as phase-separated and elementally segregated. It is unclear whether the baseline is a successfully formed single phase or a failed synthesis state.
